thread.title: New records show Walters offered $50K in bonuses to chief of staff on top of $190K salary - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: New records show Walters offered $50K in bonuses to chief of staff on top of $190K salary - NewsBreak

author: Spencer Humphrey/KFOR
title: New records show Walters offered $50K in bonuses to chief of staff on top of $190K salary - NewsBreak
text:
By Spencer Humphrey/KFOR ,
1 hours ago
OKLAHOMA CITY ( KFOR ) — News 4 has uncovered even more records showing former State Superintendent Ryan Walters paid his executive staff massive bonuses—this time, offering his chief of staff yearly bonuses worth more than the average Oklahoma teacher makes in a year, on top of a nearly $200,000 salary.
A new batch of open records obtained by News 4 includes employment documents for Walters’ chief of staff, Matt Mohler.
Walters hired Mohler as chief of staff at the beginning of 2025.
News 4 previously revealed Mohler was a Florida-based campaign consultant still actively employed by a Florida company at the time he joined OSDE in February.
In April, News 4 sent OSDE an open records request asking for copies of Mohler’s job description, employment contract and job offer letter.
New records raise ethical questions about Walters-era spending, gifts and ties to group he now works for At the time, Walters’ staff provided only the job description, claimed there was no employment agreement, and refused to release his job offer letter—arguing it would “constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.”
After State Superintendent Lindel Fields took office last month, News 4 requested those same records again.
This time, OSDE provided the offer letter.
What it says may explain why Walters’ staff were so hesitant to share it.
The letter offers Mohler a base salary of $190,000 a year to serve as Walters’ chief of staff.
It also says the position comes with quarterly bonuses of up to $12,500 each, totaling $50,000 a year in potential bonuses.
By comparison, the average starting salary for an Oklahoma teacher ranges from $40,000 to $50,000.
To former Oklahoma House Education Committee Chair Mark McBride, it’s appalling.
“It’s disgusting and it should be to every taxpayer in the state of Oklahoma—that that was allowed to happen,” McBride said.
Former Norman High School teacher suing OSDE, Ryan Walters over revoked license To former Assistant Oklahoma Attorney General and former state school board member Tim Gilpin, it’s suspicious.
“Large bonuses and offer letter, and certainly an additional large bonuses is very unusual. I have not heard of it before. And it doesn’t pass the smell test to me,” Gilpin said.
Mohler’s wasn’t the only Walters-era offer letter that included bonuses.
A January 2024 offer letter to then-OSDE CFO Spencer Wood offered him $5,000 and $10,000 yearly bonuses on top of his $125,000 base salary.
“I cannot remember hearing about a bonus of anything near this, and it appears like the State Department of Education was being run like some sort of private, single held company with state money,” Gilpin said.
“I tried to bring this to the attention of Speaker McCall our last term, last two years we were in session—and it fell on deaf ears,” McBride said.
In the summer of 2024, McBride and two dozen other House Republicans signed onto a letter asking for an investigation that could lead to Walters’ impeachment.
With House Democrats also on board, a majority of House members supported doing it.
But then-House Speaker Charles McCall said he wouldn’t consider an investigation unless many more Republicans signed on.
“We knew that this was going on, the misuse of tax dollars, the wasteful, the bonuses,” McBride said. “Why couldn’t we have started working on this a year ago, two years ago, three years ago? Why?”
That—along with all the other reports News 4 has brought recently about Walters’ extravagant staff bonuses, gifts, and other ethically questionable decisions—leaves both McBride and Gilpin hoping the State Auditor and State Ethics Commission’s ongoing investigations into Walters are thorough.
“I am a Republican and I’m embarrassed by it—that we allowed this to happen,” McBride said. “Ryan Walters is just the gift that keeps on giving,” Gilpin said. “I’m sorry to say that I think we’re going to continue to uncover things under stones.”
